messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a weird spike yesterday on a dedicated tenant after a node preempt. traffic stayed healthy for ~30s (soft-burst) then we got a cascade of 429s across the tenant. anyone run into flaky enforcement during infra churn?

alex: saw similar once when autoscaler moved pods and our quota agent briefly returned stale remaining counts. thought we had lease invalidation but maybe not.

sasha: is this the fail-open behavior we've talked about? iirc we allow soft bursts during transient failures to avoid mass-denies, but here it seemed to flip to strict and slam.

maria: yes — request flow looked like: prefix cache hit -> allowed -> then quota agent said limit exceeded and we started returning 429s even for warm connections.

kevin: couple angles: (1) where quota decisions are made (edge router vs control plane cache); (2) whether burst credits live with tenant state or per-key; (3) how long our "grace window" is. we need metrics for all 3.

sasha: agree. propose we add two short telemetry counters: `quota.enforcement_transition` (values: soft->strict, strict->soft) and `quota.drop_reason` (labels: preempt, stale-cache, overcommit). then we can see correlation with node events.

alex: +1. also add traces that include the quota decision header in responses so we can map which requests saw a change. e.g. header: ```X-Quota-Mode: soft; X-Quota-Decision: deny; X-Burst-Remaining: 0```

maria: i've got a minimal reproducer: replaying steady traffic, then kill one inference node. within 20s the tenant drains burst credits and then we get 429s for ~2m until autoscaler brings capacity back. link: https://rw-internal/issue/1234 (repro steps included)

ops-bot: cluster-event: node/preempt detected in eu-west-1 at 1991112250, migrated 3 pods

kevin: sounds like burst credits are global per-tenant and not rebalanced on capacity change. options: (A) make burst credits transferable across nodes, (B) extend grace window during topology changes, (C) fail-open for a small percentage of requests during upgrades.

sasha: (C) sounds appealing but risky for noisy neighbors. we should limit fail-open to requests under a short latency budget or to keys flagged as "critical" in the tenant. console UX could let customers opt in.

alex: for Dedicated we should prefer deterministic isolation by default. maybe have a "safe-fail-open" flag that's off for enterprise by default, on for low-tier tenants to reduce outage noise.

maria: also UX: show a small banner in the tenant console when we detect degraded quota health: "Your dedicated pool is under topology change — serving may be limited. Remaining burst credits: 1200". customers want visibility not surprises.

kevin: implementation plan suggestion: 1) add telemetry counters + headers (2) short-term: increase grace-window to 90s during node.preempt events behind a feature flag (3) console banner and route-level indicator (4) design long-term: shard burst credits by node groups with quick rebalance.

sasha: i'll own the console banner + opt-in toggle. alex can you own the feature flag and config? maria can you attach the reproducer + example traces to the ticket?

alex: yep. i'll create a feature-flagged rollout targeting canary tenants first. i'll also add an alert on `quota.enforcement_transition{from="soft",to="strict"} > 5/min` in the infra dashboard.

maria: putting proposed PR for telemetry + headers in a draft: https://rw-internal/pr/6789. it includes header examples and a tiny test harness. please review.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: quota-agent v2.3.1 -> canary pool at 1991112330

kevin: one more note — ensure we keep per-key semantics. per-org burst sharing is fine if tenant consents, but per-key (API keys) should still honor configured rates. let's document that in the console and API docs.

sasha: sounds good. i'll add a short blurb in the console settings and the docs PR. next sync: post canary results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
